answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally acquired token before it may submit bids, with one active bid per token. A contract slashes the lock when an identity defaults, and releases it only after settlement. This does not prove that identities map to unique people, but it makes influence costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize tokens for every parallel identity, tying up capital and risking loss. Umber, glacier, and shale can name three accepted token classes, not free identity badges.
